subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in soft-interrupt lifecycle that aborts the active model operation, commits any safe partial state, injects the new user message, and starts a context-aware continuation, or keep steering limited to runtime boundaries plus explicit run replacement?
rationale: Current steer and interrupt modes deliberately provide different safety guarantees; combining them changes transcript semantics, tool-side-effect handling, provider compatibility, and the meaning of an existing default queue mode.

options.title: Add opt-in soft interrupt
options.body: Introduce a distinct capability-negotiated mode with explicit partial-output, tool-side-effect, transcript, fallback, and continuation semantics while leaving existing steer behavior compatible.

options.title: Keep current mode split
options.body: Retain boundary-only steer and explicit interrupt as separate operations, documenting that transparent continuation is not supported.

options.title: Redefine steer globally
options.body: Make existing steer abort and continue immediately where possible, accepting a compatibility change for users relying on safe-boundary delivery.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in soft interrupt
recommendation.body: Introduce a distinct capability-negotiated mode with explicit partial-output, tool-side-effect, transcript, fallback, and continuation semantics while leaving existing steer behavior compatible.
